ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic diagram of the Earth's day and night hemispheres. The gray shaded part on the left indicates the night hemisphere, and the white part on the right indicates the day hemisphere. The day-night boundary is roughly located at the arc line slightly to the left in the figure. Point 1 is located near the upper terminator and is marked “66°34′N”; point 2 is located near the lower terminator; point 3 is located at the edge position of the white day hemisphere on the right; an arc line is drawn between point 2 and point 3, and point 4 is marked near the middle of this arc line. Reasoning: The question stem says that the sunrise and sunset times of points 2 and 3 are fixed and unchanged throughout the year, indicating that the day and night lengths of the two points are 12 hours throughout the year, so 2 and 3 should be located on the equator. Also because 2 is near the terminator, and the longitude difference between 2 and 3 is 90°, the meridian where 3 is located, which differs from the terminator by 90°, is the noon meridian, that is, the meridian where the direct solar point is located. The question stem also says that points 1 and 3 have the same local time, indicating that 1 and 3 are on the same meridian; and the dates on the two sides of the arc line on which they are located are different, indicating that this meridian is the 180° meridian among the date boundary lines. Therefore, the longitude of the direct solar point is 180°. In terms of latitude, the 66°34′N position in the figure corresponds to the vicinity of the Arctic Circle, and the high-latitude area of the Northern Hemisphere is located on the night hemisphere side, indicating that polar night occurs at the Arctic Circle. At this time, the Sun directly shines on the Tropic of Capricorn, namely 23°26′S. Combining longitude and latitude, the coordinates of the direct solar point are (23°26′S,180°).

raw_record.original_question:
图中阴影区域为夜半球，1、3两点的地方时刻相同但其所在弧线两侧的日期不同，2、3两点日出、日落时间全年固定不变且两点的经度差为90°；4为2、3两点之间弧线的中点。读图回答：

<image1>

此时，太阳直射点的坐标是？
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a schematic diagram of the Earth's day and night hemispheres. The gray shaded part on the left indicates the night hemisphere, and the white part on the right indicates the day hemisphere. The day-night boundary is roughly located at the arc line slightly to the left in the figure. Point 1 is located near the upper terminator and is marked “66°34′N”; point 2 is located near the lower terminator; point 3 is located at the edge position of the white day hemisphere on the right; an arc line is drawn between point 2 and point 3, and point 4 is marked near the middle of this arc line.

Reasoning: The question stem says that the sunrise and sunset times of points 2 and 3 are fixed and unchanged throughout the year, indicating that the day and night lengths of the two points are 12 hours throughout the year, so 2 and 3 should be located on the equator. Also because 2 is near the terminator, and the longitude difference between 2 and 3 is 90°, the meridian where 3 is located, which differs from the terminator by 90°, is the noon meridian, that is, the meridian where the direct solar point is located. The question stem also says that points 1 and 3 have the same local time, indicating that 1 and 3 are on the same meridian; and the dates on the two sides of the arc line on which they are located are different, indicating that this meridian is the 180° meridian among the date boundary lines. Therefore, the longitude of the direct solar point is 180°. In terms of latitude, the 66°34′N position in the figure corresponds to the vicinity of the Arctic Circle, and the high-latitude area of the Northern Hemisphere is located on the night hemisphere side, indicating that polar night occurs at the Arctic Circle. At this time, the Sun directly shines on the Tropic of Capricorn, namely 23°26′S. Combining longitude and latitude, the coordinates of the direct solar point are (23°26′S,180°).
